text: Psalm 64 For the Music Director. A Psalm of David. Hear my voice, O God, in my complaint; guard my life from dread of the enemy.
Hide me from the secret counsel of the wicked, from the throng of the workers of iniquity;
they sharpen their tongue like a sword, and bend their bows to shoot their arrows—bitter words,
that they may shoot in secret at the blameless; suddenly they shoot at him and do not fear.
They harden themselves in an evil matter; they talk privately of laying snares; they say, “Who will see them?”
They devise injustice, saying “We have perfected a secret plot.” Both the inward thought of man and the heart are deep.
But God will suddenly shoot them with an arrow; they will be wounded.
They will bring ruin on themselves by their own tongues; all who see them will flee away.
All people will fear, and declare the work of God; they will wisely consider His deeds.
The righteous will be glad in the Lord, and seek refuge in Him, and all the upright in heart will glory.
